trust_decision.summary: Request-derived values (raw query params copied into the consent data model, the request path/query as form target) are trusted as safe HTML when the FreeMarker wap consent template interpolates them without ?html; no auto-escaping is configured.

landing_point.why: Advisory names the wap consent page; the wap authorize.ftl is the only template with bare ${...} interpolations next to ?html-escaped siblings.

fix_sites.module_kind: Java data-model producer (sets server-side display_scope so the query param can no longer shadow it)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: openam-oauth2/src/main/java/org/forgerock/oauth2/restlet/ConsentRequiredResource.java:79-80 (data model seeded from request attributes + raw query; fix adds server-set display_scope at fix.diff:30-33)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Java data-model builder already ESAPI-encodes display_name/description/scopes, so a solver can argue the template is the only layer to touch and never notice that display_scope is never set server-side and is filled from the raw query map.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: popup.ftl intentionally emits the rendered authorize.ftl HTML raw via ${htmlCode}, and page/touch/popup templates emit pre-encoded JSON raw (${display_scopes}, ${display_claims}); a global ?html / auto-escape fix breaks the popup display and the XUI consent JS; display_name/display_description are already ESAPI-encoded in Java so escaping them again in the template double-encodes.

O6_input_shapes: scalar query parameter in HTML attribute (response_type, client_id)
request path+query reflected as form action (target)
sequence item in #list (display_scope), previously attacker-supplied via query map
values re-injected from a stored device code into request attributes (device/user flow)

O7_producer.where: openam-oauth2/src/main/java/org/forgerock/oauth2/restlet/DeviceCodeVerificationResource.java:239-257 (stored device-code attributes copied into request attributes, which ConsentRequiredResource.java:79 copies into the template model)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second display variant (touch/page) emitting a model value with ?html or bare instead of ?js_string inside the script block
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Four near-duplicate display templates are maintained by hand; a maintainer adding a field to one copy could choose the wrong escaper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: user_name is put into the model unencoded; a wap template line showing ${user_name} would be a realistic distant sibling
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Other display_* fields are pre-encoded in Java while user_name is not, so a template author could assume all model values are pre-encoded.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a stored device-code attribute (e.g. state/acr) rendered bare in the wap form, reached only through the device/user save-reload path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Device-code attributes are replayed as request attributes and land in the same model without passing the query path a solver reproduces.
